intro: This week's five themes: a genuine SCLC signal buried inside a mis-tagged bispecific-ADC readout, a new PRMT5/KRAS G12D combination lane in pancreatic cancer, the first Phase 3 win for personalized mRNA cancer vaccines, AI platforms entering life-sciences drug design, and a quiet dealmaking cycle anchored by Amgen's TScan exit.

narratives.headline: iza-bren's SCLC dose-expansion data separates from its NSCLC tagging noise as a real 2L signal
narratives.detail: BL-B01D1 (iza-bren), the Biokin/BMS EGFRxHER3 bispecific ADC, generated six indication tags this cycle from one lung-cancer press item, but its small-cell lung cancer occurrence checks out as a separate, real signal. A Phase Ib ES-SCLC dose-expansion readout (NCT05194982) reported 2L-subgroup ORR of 72.7%, mPFS 6.2 months, and mOS 15.0 months. If those numbers hold under primary-source verification, they would beat the 2L+ bar set by both lurbinectedin (ORR 35%) and tarlatamab (ORR 40%). The asset genuinely runs separate NSCLC, breast, and SCLC trials — a case where multi-indication development is real rather than a triage mis-tag.

narratives.headline: IDEAYA and Genentech pair a PRMT5 inhibitor with a KRAS G12D inhibitor in MTAP-deleted pancreatic cancer
narratives.detail: IDEAYA's IDE892 (PRMT5 inhibitor) and Genentech's RG6620 (KRAS G12D inhibitor) entered a clinical collaboration targeting MTAP-deleted, KRAS G12D-mutant PDAC. It's a sibling combination lane to the already-reported vopimetostat plus daraxonrasib readout in PDAC, which posted a 92% ORR, reinforcing MTAP-deletion synthetic lethality as a target multiple sponsors are converging on. No NCT number, phase, or efficacy data has been disclosed for the new combination itself.

narratives.headline: Merck and Moderna's personalized neoantigen mRNA cancer vaccine posts its first Phase 3 win
narratives.detail: Intismeran autogene, Merck and Moderna's individualized neoantigen mRNA vaccine, delivered the class's first confirmatory Phase 3 result — new momentum for the modality broadly. The result resurfaced later in the tracking window only as a duplicate wire pickup, with no additional data attached beyond the original readout.

narratives.headline: Anthropic's Claude and SandboxAQ's AQPotency both landed as AI-platform entrants in life sciences this week
narratives.detail: Two independent signals arrived in one cycle: a Claude-overseen research campaign designed miniproteins from scratch, and SandboxAQ launched AQPotency, a structure-free drug-potency prediction model, with Claude/MCP availability built in. Both name Anthropic infrastructure directly, arriving alongside the FDA's ongoing generative-AI-device discussion paper as backdrop. No clinical or regulatory outcome is attached to either yet.

narratives.headline: A quiet week for new pharma dealmaking, with Amgen's TScan exit the standout move
narratives.detail: Amgen exited its T-cell-therapy partnership with TScan Therapeutics, part of a broader biotech-dealmaking roundup that also touched BioArctic, Enveda, Georgiamune, Kynexis, Tolerance Bio, and Network Bio. Separately, Tolerance Bio and NeoImmuneTech signed a deal worth up to $260M for a thymus-targeting fusion protein entering Phase 2, and Piramal Pharma acquired a majority stake in Yapan Bio, a Phase I/II CDMO for vaccines and biologics. None of the disclosed deals touch a clinical asset in the tracked landscape.
